category: Definitions II: functions, selections, couplings, probes, coordinate systems & moving mesh
description: The remaining Global Definitions and Component > Definitions nodes: the full set of built-in function types (ramp, rectangle, pulses, waves, random, elevation, image, external C and MATLAB functions, surrogate models), geometric and Boolean selections, nonlocal coupling operators, probes, coordinate systems, infinite elements, mass properties, pairs and the Free Deformation / Prescribed Deformation / Rotating Domain moving-mesh definition features. API calls use model.func() for global functions, model.component("comp1").selection(), .cpl(), .probe(), .coordSystem(), .pair(), .massProp() and .common() for component-level definitions.

tools.name: Ramp
tools.description: Global function that is zero up to a location and then rises linearly with a given slope, optionally saturating at a cutoff value. The classic way to bring a load, voltage or inlet velocity in gradually so a time-dependent or continuation solve starts from a consistent state. Smoothing options round the corner at the location and at the cutoff so the derivative is continuous.
tools.usage: Global Definitions > Functions > Ramp (rm1); API: model.func().create("rm1", "Ramp")

parameters.name: location
parameters.description: Argument value where the ramp starts (default 0).

parameters.name: slope
parameters.description: Rate of increase per unit argument (default 1).

parameters.name: cutoffactive / cutoff
parameters.description: Enable and set the value at which the ramp levels off.

parameters.name: smooth / smoothzoneloc
parameters.description: Size of the smoothing zone at the start (and cutoff) in argument units and the number of continuous derivatives.

tools.notes: The function is dimensionless; multiply by the physical amplitude and pass a unitless argument such as t[1/s]. Use Step for an instantaneous switch and Rectangle for a finite pulse.

tools.name: Rectangle (function)
tools.description: Box-car function equal to a given amplitude between a lower and an upper limit and zero elsewhere, with optional smoothing of both transitions. Used for pulses in time (a heating pulse, a voltage burst) or for switching a source on over a spatial interval.
tools.usage: Global Definitions > Functions > Rectangle (rect1); API: model.func().create("rect1", "Rectangle")

parameters.name: lower / upper
parameters.description: Interval limits in the argument variable.

parameters.name: amplitude
parameters.description: Function value inside the interval (default 1).

parameters.name: smooth
parameters.description: Enable smoothing and set the transition zone size and the number of continuous derivatives.

tools.notes: For a sharp pulse make sure the time-dependent solver takes steps inside the pulse (set Steps taken by solver to Strict or add the pulse times to the output list). The related Triangle function gives a tent-shaped pulse and Gaussian Pulse a bell-shaped one.

tools.name: Triangle
tools.description: Tent-shaped function rising linearly from zero at the lower limit to the amplitude at the midpoint and back to zero at the upper limit. A convenient C0 pulse for excitations and for building hat-function weightings.
tools.usage: Global Definitions > Functions > Triangle (tri1); API: model.func().create("tri1", "Triangle")

parameters.name: lower / upper
parameters.description: Support of the pulse.

parameters.name: amplitude
parameters.description: Peak value at the midpoint.

parameters.name: smooth
parameters.description: Optional smoothing of the three corners.

tools.notes: Available since 6.0; in older models the same shape was built from a Piecewise function.

tools.name: Gaussian Pulse
tools.description: Bell-shaped function exp(-(x-x0)^2/(2 sigma^2)) centred at a location with standard deviation sigma, normalised either to unit integral (the default, useful as a smooth delta approximation) or to a given peak value. Typical uses are laser or beam heat sources in space, short excitation pulses in time for transient acoustics and electromagnetics, and initial conditions.
tools.usage: Global Definitions > Functions > Gaussian Pulse (gp1); API: model.func().create("gp1", "GaussianPulse")

parameters.name: location
parameters.description: Centre x0 of the pulse.

parameters.name: sigma
parameters.description: Standard deviation controlling the width.

parameters.name: normalization
parameters.description: integral (area 1, peak 1/(sigma*sqrt(2*pi))) or peak (peak value set by peakvalue).

tools.notes: Give the argument unit in the Units section of the function (or keep everything dimensionless) so the plot preview and the physics agree; for a 2D radial profile use gp1(sqrt(x^2+y^2)).

tools.name: Wave
tools.description: Periodic waveform generator producing a sine, square, sawtooth or triangle wave of given period, amplitude and phase, optionally with smoothing of square/sawtooth edges and a modulation option. Handy for PWM drive signals, AC excitation in the time domain and cyclic loads.
tools.usage: Global Definitions > Functions > Wave (wv1); API: model.func().create("wv1", "Wave")

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: sine | square | sawtooth | triangle.

parameters.name: period / amplitude / phase
parameters.description: Waveform period in argument units, peak amplitude and phase shift.

parameters.name: smooth
parameters.description: Smoothing zone for the discontinuities of square and sawtooth waves.

tools.notes: For a plain sinusoid in a frequency-domain study you do not need this; use the built-in complex amplitude. Time-domain square waves need Strict or Intermediate time stepping to resolve the edges.

tools.name: Random
tools.description: Function returning a pseudo-random value for each distinct argument value, drawn from a uniform distribution over a range or from a normal distribution with given mean and standard deviation. Because the value is a deterministic hash of the argument (and the seed), the same argument always gives the same number, so it can be used inside expressions for surface roughness, random initial conditions or Monte-Carlo style parameter sweeps.
tools.usage: Global Definitions > Functions > Random (rn1); API: model.func().create("rn1", "Random")

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: uniform | normal distribution.

parameters.name: mean
parameters.description: Mean value of the distribution.

parameters.name: uniformrange / normalsigma
parameters.description: Width of the uniform interval or the standard deviation of the normal distribution.

parameters.name: nargs / seed
parameters.description: Number of arguments and the random seed controlling the sequence.

tools.notes: The function is not differentiable, so avoid it in expressions the solver must linearize; use nojac(rn1(...)) or evaluate it only in initial values. Use the Normal Distribution function when you want the probability density itself rather than samples.

tools.name: Normal Distribution
tools.description: Function evaluating the normal (Gaussian) probability density with given mean and standard deviation. Used for size distributions of particles or bubbles, dopant profiles and weighting functions where the density value, not a random sample, is needed.
tools.usage: Global Definitions > Functions > Normal Distribution (nd1); API: model.func().create("nd1", "NormalDistribution")

parameters.name: mean
parameters.description: Centre of the distribution.

parameters.name: sigma
parameters.description: Standard deviation.

tools.notes: Related: Gaussian Pulse (same shape, chosen by peak or area) and the Random function (samples).

tools.name: Elevation (DEM)
tools.description: Function that reads a digital elevation model file (USGS DEM, GeoTIFF, ASCII grid, ESRI and similar formats) and returns terrain height as a function of two horizontal coordinates. It is used to build topography-following geometry (Parametric Surface driven by the function), for terrain-aware heat transfer, groundwater and acoustics models and for background elevation in ray tracing.
tools.usage: Global Definitions > Functions > Elevation (elev1); API: model.func().create("elev1", "Elevation")

parameters.name: filename
parameters.description: Path to the DEM file; use importData() to embed the data in the model.

parameters.name: interp / extrap
parameters.description: Interpolation (nearest, linear, cubic) and extrapolation (constant, linear, specific value) settings.

parameters.name: Units
parameters.description: Unit of the returned elevation and of the coordinate arguments.

tools.notes: Large rasters are expensive to evaluate at every Gauss point; coarsen the DEM or restrict the parametric surface resolution. The Image function does the same thing for bitmap files (grey level as a function of x, y).

tools.name: Image (function)
tools.description: Function that maps a bitmap image (BMP, GIF, JPEG, PNG or TIFF) onto a 2D coordinate range and returns a scaled grey-level value at (x, y). It is the quick route from a micrograph, MRI slice or drawn pattern to a spatially varying material property, a mask for topology optimization or a source distribution; the Image to Curve add-in and mphimage2geom go one step further and turn the image into geometry.
tools.usage: Global Definitions > Functions > Image (im1); API: model.func().create("im1", "Image")

parameters.name: filename
parameters.description: Image file; importData() stores it in the model.

parameters.name: scaling
parameters.description: How grey levels map to the output range (e.g. 0-1 or a custom min/max).

parameters.name: xmin/xmax/ymin/ymax
parameters.description: Coordinate box the image is stretched over.

parameters.name: flipx / flipy / inplace
parameters.description: Mirror the image or evaluate directly on the pixel grid.

tools.notes: Only 2D arguments are supported; for 3D stacks use an Interpolation function with a data file. Pixel steps are discontinuous, so use nojac() or smoothing if the value enters a Jacobian.

tools.name: External (C function)
tools.description: Function implemented in a shared library (DLL on Windows, .so on Linux, .dylib on macOS) written in C, with optional derivative and initialisation callbacks. Use it for proprietary material models, legacy code or expensive kernels that must run natively; COMSOL calls the library at every evaluation point with arrays of argument values.
tools.usage: Global Definitions > Functions > External (extf1); API: model.func().create("extf1", "External")

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: Path to the compiled shared library.

parameters.name: funcs
parameters.description: Table of function names in the library and the number of arguments each takes.

parameters.name: init
parameters.description: Optional initialisation string passed to the library's init function.

parameters.name: ders
parameters.description: Whether the library also provides derivative functions (needed for Newton convergence).

tools.notes: The library must export the eval/init/error entry points described in the Reference Manual chapter on External Functions and must be compiled for the same architecture as COMSOL. External Material (Materials branch) is the equivalent mechanism for full user-defined constitutive laws.

tools.name: MATLAB (function)
tools.description: Declares one or more MATLAB functions that COMSOL calls through LiveLink for MATLAB whenever the expression is evaluated, passing argument arrays and receiving result arrays. This lets material properties, boundary conditions or sources be computed by arbitrary MATLAB code, including toolbox calls, at the cost of a round trip per evaluation.
tools.usage: Global Definitions > Functions > MATLAB (mlf1); API: model.func().create("mlf1", "MATLAB")

parameters.name: funcs
parameters.description: Table of MATLAB function names and their argument lists, e.g. {"myk", "T"}.

parameters.name: ders
parameters.description: Optional table naming MATLAB functions that return the derivatives with respect to each argument.

parameters.name: Clear functions
parameters.description: Setting that forces MATLAB to reload the .m file after edits.

tools.notes: Requires LiveLink for MATLAB and a running MATLAB session (start COMSOL with MATLAB, or comsol mphserver matlab). The .m function must be vectorised, since COMSOL passes arrays. Without derivative functions COMSOL uses finite differences, which slows Newton iterations.

tools.name: Least-Squares Fit
tools.description: Function that fits a user-chosen parametric expression to tabulated or imported data by least squares and then behaves like an Analytic function of the fitted form. Use it to convert measured material data (e.g. conductivity versus temperature) into a smooth closed-form expression with well-defined derivatives instead of an interpolation table.
tools.usage: Global Definitions > Functions > Least-Squares Fit (lsq1); API: model.func().create("lsq1", "LeastSquares")

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: table | file - where the data points come from.

parameters.name: args
parameters.description: Function argument names (the x columns).

parameters.name: exprs
parameters.description: The fit expression with unknown fit parameters, e.g. a + b*T + c*T^2.

parameters.name: columnType / parameters
parameters.description: Column roles (argument / value / weight) and the names, initial guesses and bounds of the fit parameters.

tools.notes: The fitted parameter values are shown in the settings window after import and can be copied into Parameters. Related: Interpolation (piecewise), Partial Fraction Fit (rational fits for frequency-domain data), and the surrogate model functions.

tools.name: Function Switch
tools.description: Container that holds several alternative function definitions under one name and exposes a switch index selecting which one is active. Combined with a Function Sweep study step it lets one model be solved for several candidate excitation profiles or material curves without editing expressions.
tools.usage: Global Definitions > Functions > Switch (funcsw1) with nested Analytic / Interpolation / Piecewise children; API: model.func().create("funcsw1", "FunctionSwitch")

parameters.name: Nested functions
parameters.description: Child functions that must share the same name and argument list.

parameters.name: Switch value
parameters.description: Index of the active case, set manually or by a Function Sweep.

tools.notes: The Material Switch node under Materials plays the same role for whole materials, driven by a Material Sweep.

tools.name: Gaussian Process (surrogate model)
tools.description: Surrogate-model function trained on a table of input/output samples (typically produced by a Surrogate Model Training study or a design-of-experiments sweep) using Gaussian process regression (kriging). Once trained it evaluates in microseconds and also returns a standard deviation, so it can replace an expensive full model inside apps, optimisation loops and uncertainty quantification.
tools.usage: Global Definitions > Functions > Gaussian Process (gp1); API: model.func().create("gp1", "GaussianProcess")

parameters.name: Data source
parameters.description: Table, file or the results table of a Surrogate Model Training study.

parameters.name: covfunction / meanfunction
parameters.description: Kernel (squared exponential, Matern) and trend model.

parameters.name: validation
parameters.description: Hold-out fraction or cross-validation settings used to report the fit quality.

parameters.name: definestddev
parameters.description: Also expose the predicted standard deviation as a separate function.

tools.notes: Requires the Uncertainty Quantification Module (6.1+). Alternatives: Polynomial Chaos Expansion for smooth global fits, Deep Neural Network for large data sets.

tools.name: Deep Neural Network (surrogate model)
tools.description: Surrogate function implemented as a fully connected neural network trained in COMSOL on sampled model data, with configurable layers, activation functions, optimiser, epochs and optional GPU training. Suited to high-dimensional input spaces and large training sets where kriging becomes expensive; used inside apps, digital twins and optimisation.
tools.usage: Global Definitions > Functions > Deep Neural Network (dnn1); API: model.func().create("dnn1", "DNN")

parameters.name: layertype / outfeatures
parameters.description: Architecture: layer types and widths, number of outputs.

parameters.name: epochs / optmethod
parameters.description: Training length and optimiser (Adam, etc.).

parameters.name: gputraining
parameters.description: Use a CUDA GPU for training when available.

parameters.name: validation
parameters.description: Validation split reported as loss curves.

tools.notes: Requires the Uncertainty Quantification Module (6.2+). Training data normally comes from Study > Surrogate Model Training, which writes to a results table the function reads.

tools.name: Ball (selection)
tools.description: Geometric selection that picks all entities of a chosen level (domains, boundaries, edges or points) whose location lies inside, or intersects, a sphere of given centre and radius. Like Box it is evaluated after the geometry is built, so it keeps working when entity numbers change during a parametric geometry sweep.
tools.usage: Component > Definitions > Selections > Ball (ball1); API: model.component("comp1").selection().create("ball1", "Ball")

parameters.name: entitydim
parameters.description: 3 domain, 2 boundary, 1 edge, 0 point.

parameters.name: posx/posy/posz, r
parameters.description: Centre coordinates and radius.

parameters.name: condition
parameters.description: inside | intersects | allvertices - how much of an entity must lie in the ball.

tools.notes: Cylinder and Disk selections use the same mechanism with different shapes. In 2D the ball degenerates to a circle.

tools.name: Cylinder (selection)
tools.description: Geometric selection of entities inside a finite cylinder defined by a point on the axis, an axis direction, a radius and top/bottom distances. Typical for selecting all boundaries of a bore hole, the windings of a coil or an annular region without clicking each face.
tools.usage: Component > Definitions > Selections > Cylinder (cyl1); API: model.component("comp1").selection().create("cyl1", "Cylinder")

parameters.name: entitydim
parameters.description: Entity level to select.

parameters.name: posx/posy/posz, axis
parameters.description: Axis reference point and direction (x, y, z or custom vector).

parameters.name: r, rin, top, bottom
parameters.description: Outer radius, optional inner radius (annulus), and axial extent.

parameters.name: condition
parameters.description: inside | intersects | allvertices.

tools.notes: In 2D use Disk; in 2D axisymmetry a Box selection in (r, z) is usually simpler.

tools.name: Disk (selection)
tools.description: 2D counterpart of the Cylinder selection: picks domains, boundaries or points inside a circle (or annulus) of given centre and radii. Also available in 3D for selecting entities lying in a circular disk on a plane.
tools.usage: Component > Definitions > Selections > Disk (disk1); API: model.component("comp1").selection().create("disk1", "Disk")

parameters.name: entitydim
parameters.description: Entity level.

parameters.name: posx/posy, r, rin
parameters.description: Centre, outer radius and optional inner radius.

parameters.name: condition
parameters.description: inside | intersects | allvertices.

tools.notes: Related: Ball, Cylinder, Box (rectangular).

tools.name: Complement (selection)
tools.description: Boolean selection containing every entity of the given level that is not in the input selections. The usual way to express 'all other boundaries' for a default condition, or 'everything except the coil' for the air domain when the coil selection already exists.
tools.usage: Component > Definitions > Selections > Complement (comp1sel); API: model.component("comp1").selection().create("compl1", "Complement")

parameters.name: entitydim
parameters.description: Entity level; all inputs must be of this level.

parameters.name: input
parameters.description: Tags of the selections to complement.

tools.notes: Related Boolean selections: Union, Intersection, Difference. Adjacent gives the neighbours of a selection rather than its complement.

tools.name: Difference (selection)
tools.description: Boolean selection equal to the entities of the 'selections to add' minus those in the 'selections to subtract'. Lets you derive, say, 'outer walls' as 'all boundaries' minus 'inlet' minus 'outlet' so that the result follows geometry changes automatically.
tools.usage: Component > Definitions > Selections > Difference (dif1); API: model.component("comp1").selection().create("dif1", "Difference")

parameters.name: entitydim
parameters.description: Entity level.

parameters.name: add
parameters.description: Selections to include.

parameters.name: subtract
parameters.description: Selections to remove.

tools.notes: Selections created in the Geometry sequence (e.g. by the Selections of Resulting Entities option of a primitive) are referenced with tags like geom1_blk1_bnd.

tools.name: Union (selection)
tools.description: Boolean selection that merges several selections of the same entity level into one, so a single named selection can be used in physics features, probes and plots. Common for collecting all heat-sink fins or all electrodes defined by separate geometry features.
tools.usage: Component > Definitions > Selections > Union (uni1); API: model.component("comp1").selection().create("uni1", "Union")

parameters.name: entitydim
parameters.description: Entity level.

parameters.name: input
parameters.description: Selections to merge.

tools.notes: Intersection returns only entities common to all inputs; Difference subtracts.

tools.name: Intersection (selection)
tools.description: Boolean selection holding only the entities present in every input selection. Useful for combining a geometric filter with a topological one, e.g. 'boundaries of the coil' intersected with 'boundaries inside this box' to get the coil end faces.
tools.usage: Component > Definitions > Selections > Intersection (int1); API: model.component("comp1").selection().create("int1", "Intersection")

parameters.name: entitydim
parameters.description: Entity level.

parameters.name: input
parameters.description: Selections to intersect.

tools.notes: Related: Adjacent (boundaries of a domain selection), Union, Difference, Complement.

tools.name: Average (aveop)
tools.description: Nonlocal coupling operator that returns the average of an expression over a source selection (domains, boundaries, edges or points), i.e. the integral divided by the measure of the selection. The operator can be used anywhere in the model - in physics settings, variables, probes and results - which is what makes it a coupling: a boundary condition can depend on the mean temperature of another region.
tools.usage: Component > Definitions > Nonlocal Couplings > Average (aveop1); API: model.component("comp1").cpl().create("aveop1", "Average")

parameters.name: Source selection
parameters.description: Entities averaged over; set entitydim and selection().

parameters.name: axisym
parameters.description: Include the 2*pi*r factor in 2D axisymmetric models.

parameters.name: frame
parameters.description: Spatial or material frame for the measure.

parameters.name: opname
parameters.description: Operator name used in expressions (default aveop1).

tools.notes: Integration (intop) gives the raw integral; Maximum/Minimum return extreme values. Averaging a quantity that also depends on the unknown couples every DOF in the source to the destination, producing a dense Jacobian block - use nojac() around the operator if the dependence can be lagged.

tools.name: Maximum (maxop)
tools.description: Nonlocal coupling operator returning the maximum of an expression over the source selection, evaluated at element Gauss/Lagrange points. The optional second argument lets you evaluate one expression at the location where another is maximal, maxop1(T, x). Used for peak stress or temperature constraints in optimization, stop conditions and probes.
tools.usage: Component > Definitions > Nonlocal Couplings > Maximum (maxop1); API: model.component("comp1").cpl().create("maxop1", "Maximum")

parameters.name: Source selection
parameters.description: Entities searched.

parameters.name: Point type
parameters.description: Lagrange points or Gauss points used for the search (controls accuracy versus cost).

parameters.name: opname
parameters.description: Operator name.

tools.notes: Not differentiable, so use it in objective functions only with derivative-free optimizers or via nojac(). Results > Derived Values > Volume Maximum does the same thing for postprocessing without a coupling.

tools.name: Minimum (minop)
tools.description: Nonlocal coupling operator returning the minimum of an expression over a selection; syntax and settings mirror Maximum, including the two-argument form minop1(expr, evalexpr) to evaluate a second quantity where the first is minimal. Typical uses: minimum safety factor, minimum film thickness, lowest temperature for a freezing check.
tools.usage: Component > Definitions > Nonlocal Couplings > Minimum (minop1); API: model.component("comp1").cpl().create("minop1", "Minimum")

parameters.name: Source selection
parameters.description: Entities searched.

parameters.name: Point type
parameters.description: Lagrange or Gauss points.

tools.notes: See Maximum for the differentiability caveat.

tools.name: Linear Extrusion (linext)
tools.description: Coupling operator that maps values from a source selection to a destination through an affine transformation defined by up to four point pairs (source vertex i maps to destination vertex i). It is the simple, robust way to copy a field between two parallel faces, mirror across a symmetry plane, or map a 2D cross-section solution onto a 3D extruded body without writing the transformation expressions needed by General Extrusion.
tools.usage: Component > Definitions > Nonlocal Couplings > Linear Extrusion (linext1); API: model.component("comp1").cpl().create("linext1", "LinearExtrusion")

parameters.name: Source selection
parameters.description: Where the expression is evaluated.

parameters.name: Source vertices 1-4 / Destination vertices 1-4
parameters.description: Point pairs (or coordinates) defining the affine map; the number needed depends on the dimension.

parameters.name: Use source map / mesh search
parameters.description: Destination map options when source and destination are in different geometries.

tools.notes: Periodic Condition physics features already use an extrusion internally; use Linear Extrusion when you need the mapped value in an expression rather than a constraint. General Extrusion handles arbitrary, nonlinear mappings.

tools.name: General Projection (genproj)
tools.description: Coupling operator that integrates an expression along one coordinate direction (defined by source and destination map expressions) and returns the result as a function on the lower-dimensional destination - effectively a line integral 'through' a domain. Use it for depth-integrated quantities (total current through a cross-section as a function of x, optical thickness, column-averaged concentration) and for shadowing/projection in radiation.
tools.usage: Component > Definitions > Nonlocal Couplings > General Projection (genproj1); API: model.component("comp1").cpl().create("genproj1", "GeneralProjection")

parameters.name: Source selection
parameters.description: Domain integrated over.

parameters.name: Source map x1, x2 (x3)
parameters.description: Expressions defining the integration lines; the last coordinate is the integration direction.

parameters.name: Destination map
parameters.description: Expressions giving the destination coordinates (default the same as the first source map entries).

tools.notes: Linear Projection is the special case where the maps are defined by vertex pairs. Projections integrate over the source mesh, so coarse meshes give step-like results.

tools.name: Linear Projection (linproj)
tools.description: Projection coupling whose integration direction and destination mapping are defined by source and destination vertex pairs instead of expressions, so it needs no coordinate formulas. Typical use: integrate a 2D field in the y direction to get a 1D profile along an edge, or a 3D field through the thickness onto a face.
tools.usage: Component > Definitions > Nonlocal Couplings > Linear Projection (linproj1); API: model.component("comp1").cpl().create("linproj1", "LinearProjection")

parameters.name: Source selection
parameters.description: Entities integrated.

parameters.name: Source vertices / Destination vertices
parameters.description: Point pairs defining the affine projection.

tools.notes: See General Projection for the expression-based version.

tools.name: Boundary Similarity (bndsim)
tools.description: Extrusion coupling specialised for mapping between two boundaries that are congruent up to a rigid motion (translation and rotation), as in periodic sectors, opposite faces of a unit cell or a rotor/stator interface. COMSOL computes the transformation automatically from the boundaries themselves, so no vertex pairs or expressions are required.
tools.usage: Component > Definitions > Nonlocal Couplings > Boundary Similarity (bndsim1); API: model.component("comp1").cpl().create("bndsim1", "BoundarySimilarity")

parameters.name: Source boundaries
parameters.description: The boundary whose values are read.

parameters.name: Destination boundaries
parameters.description: The boundary the values are mapped onto (must be congruent).

parameters.name: Transformation
parameters.description: Automatic, or manual choice of which vertices correspond when ambiguous.

tools.notes: If the boundaries are not exactly congruent (different mesh is fine, different shape is not) the mapping fails; fall back to General Extrusion.

tools.name: Identity Mapping (idmap)
tools.description: Extrusion coupling that maps a point to the point with the same coordinates in another geometry or component, used to transfer fields between components of a multi-component model (e.g. a 3D thermal component and a 3D structural component built on different meshes, or 2D and 2D axisymmetric components sharing coordinates). Pairs formed by Form Assembly use the same idea internally.
tools.usage: Component > Definitions > Nonlocal Couplings > Identity Mapping (idmap1); API: model.component("comp1").cpl().create("idmap1", "IdentityMapping")

parameters.name: Source selection
parameters.description: Entities in the source component.

parameters.name: Destination
parameters.description: Component/geometry in which the operator is used; coordinates are matched one-to-one.

parameters.name: Mesh search method
parameters.description: Closest point or fail-if-outside behaviour when the destination point is not in the source mesh.

tools.notes: Operators defined in another component are referenced with the component scope prefix (comp1.idmap1). Use a General Extrusion when a coordinate transformation is needed.

tools.name: Boundary Probe
tools.description: Probe that evaluates the integral, average, maximum or minimum of an expression over a boundary selection at every solver step and stores the result in a probe table, plotting it live while solving. Standard way to monitor heat flux through a wall, drag on a surface, current through an electrode or the mean outlet temperature during a time-dependent or parametric run.
tools.usage: Component > Definitions > Probes > Boundary Probe (bnd1); API: model.component("comp1").probe().create("bnd1", "Boundary")

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: integral | average | maximum | minimum.

parameters.name: expr / unit / descr
parameters.description: Expression, output unit and table description.

parameters.name: Selection
parameters.description: Boundaries probed; axisymmetric integrals include 2*pi*r.

parameters.name: probename
parameters.description: Variable name so the probe value can be used elsewhere (default bnd1).

tools.notes: Probe values are available after solving as global variables and in the Probe Table; results with parametric sweeps produce one row per parameter and step. Domain Probe, Edge Probe and Point probes follow the same pattern.

tools.name: Global Variable Probe
tools.description: Probe that tracks any global (scalar) expression - a parameter, an integration-operator value, a lumped-port S-parameter, a terminal current or a circuit voltage - while the solver runs, with live plotting and table output. It is also the standard way to make a nonlocal quantity available to the Stop Condition node and to the Application Builder.
tools.usage: Component > Definitions > Probes > Global Variable Probe (var1); API: model.component("comp1").probe().create("var1", "GlobalVariable")

parameters.name: expr
parameters.description: Global scalar expression, e.g. es.C11, intop1(ec.Qh), cir.R1_i.

parameters.name: unit / descr
parameters.description: Output unit and description used as the table column header.

parameters.name: probename
parameters.description: Name of the resulting global variable.

tools.notes: Probe evaluation adds a little cost per step but is much cheaper than storing every solution. In MATLAB, mphglobal(model, 'var1') returns the same values after the solve.

tools.name: Boundary Point Probe
tools.description: Point probe restricted to a boundary: you give coordinates and COMSOL snaps to the closest point on the selected boundary, then evaluates an expression there at every solver step. Useful for sensor locations on a surface (thermocouple on a wall, microphone on a baffle) where a Domain Point Probe might land slightly inside the wrong domain.
tools.usage: Component > Definitions > Probes > Boundary Point Probe (bpnt1); API: model.component("comp1").probe().create("bpnt1", "BoundaryPoint")

parameters.name: Selection
parameters.description: Boundary the point is snapped to.

parameters.name: coords
parameters.description: Requested coordinates of the sensor.

parameters.name: Point Probe Expression subnode
parameters.description: One or more expressions (ppb1, ppb2...) with unit and description.

tools.notes: Domain Point Probe (already catalogued) is the interior version; both create a Point Probe Expression subnode per quantity.

tools.name: Cylindrical System
tools.description: Coordinate system with radial, azimuthal and axial base vectors about a chosen axis and origin, used to express anisotropic material properties (wound composites, laminated cores, radial fibres), loads and constraints in cylindrical components, and to define coil current directions. Physics features that take a coordinate system (Linear Elastic Material, Ampère's Law, Heat Transfer in Solids) list it once it exists.
tools.usage: Component > Definitions > Coordinate Systems > Cylindrical System (sys2); API: model.component("comp1").coordSystem().create("sys2", "Cylindrical")

parameters.name: Origin
parameters.description: Point on the axis.

parameters.name: Longitudinal axis
parameters.description: Axis direction (x, y, z or a vector).

parameters.name: Direction of axis phi = 0
parameters.description: Reference direction for the azimuth.

parameters.name: Frame
parameters.description: Spatial or material frame.

tools.notes: Other types: Rotated System (Euler angles), Spherical System, Boundary System (normal/tangent frame on boundaries), Curvilinear System (from the Curvilinear Coordinates interface), Scaling System (for PML-like stretching) and Cylindrical/Cartesian PML systems.

tools.name: Boundary System
tools.description: Local coordinate system defined on boundaries by the surface normal and two tangents (t1, t2, n), created automatically as sys1 in every component. Physics features use it to prescribe loads or displacements in normal/tangential components (e.g. a normal pressure or a tangential traction, a roller constraint) and it provides the variables nx, ny, nz, t1x... on boundaries.
tools.usage: Component > Definitions > Boundary System (sys1, automatic); API: model.component("comp1").coordSystem().create("sys2", "BoundarySystem")

parameters.name: Coordinate names
parameters.description: t1, t2, n by default.

parameters.name: Create first tangent direction from
parameters.description: Global Cartesian axis, a rotated system or a manual expression controlling the orientation of t1 on each face.

parameters.name: Reverse normal direction
parameters.description: Flip n on selected boundaries (the default normal points out of the domain with the lower number).

tools.notes: For a consistent normal direction on interior boundaries use the up/down variables or the Reverse normal option; the direction is reported in the Selection section of the settings window.

tools.name: Infinite Element Domain
tools.description: Definitions node that applies a coordinate stretching to selected outer domains so that they effectively extend to infinity, letting static and low-frequency fields (electrostatics, magnetostatics, heat conduction, Darcy flow, structural far fields) decay correctly with a small surrounding box instead of a huge air/soil region. The geometry must contain a layer of domains around the region of interest, typically made with the Layers section of a sphere/block or a separate shell.
tools.usage: Component > Definitions > Infinite Element Domain (ie1); API: model.component("comp1").coordSystem().create("ie1", "InfiniteElement")

parameters.name: Selection
parameters.description: The outer layer domains.

parameters.name: Geometry type
parameters.description: Cartesian | cylindrical | spherical | user defined - matches the layer shape.

parameters.name: Scaling
parameters.description: Physical width and pole distance of the stretching (defaults usually fine).

tools.notes: Use a Perfectly Matched Layer for wave problems instead. Mesh the infinite-element layer with a swept/mapped mesh of a few elements through the thickness, and do not evaluate results in it. Requires that the physics interface supports infinite elements (most static ones do).

tools.name: Mass Properties
tools.description: Definitions node that computes volume, mass, centre of mass and moments of inertia of a selection from the geometry and the material density (or a user expression), exposing them as variables (mass1.mass, mass1.CMx, mass1.Ixx...). Used for balancing rotors, for rigid-body inertia inputs in Multibody Dynamics, and simply to check that a CAD import has the expected mass.
tools.usage: Component > Definitions > Mass Properties (mass1); API: model.component("comp1").massProp().create("mass1", "MassProperties")

parameters.name: Selection
parameters.description: Domains included.

parameters.name: densitySource
parameters.description: From material or user-defined density expression.

parameters.name: Frame
parameters.description: Material (undeformed) or spatial (deformed) frame - the latter follows a moving mesh.

tools.notes: Evaluation needs a solution (any study) because the variables are defined through integration on the mesh; densitySource fromPhysics takes rho from the structural interface, fromMaterial from the Materials node.

tools.name: Identity Pair
tools.description: Pair node that links two boundaries which coincide in space but belong to different geometry objects in an assembly (Form Assembly), so that physics can be made continuous across them with pair-type features (Continuity, Thermal Contact, Fluid-Fluid Interface). Form Assembly creates identity pairs automatically for touching faces; you edit them to choose source and destination sides and to remove unwanted pairs.
tools.usage: Component > Definitions > Pairs > Identity Pair (p1); API: model.component("comp1").pair().create("p1", "Identity")

parameters.name: Source boundaries / Destination boundaries
parameters.description: The two sides; the destination is constrained to the source in pair features.

parameters.name: Pair type
parameters.description: Identity for continuity, Contact for structural contact.

parameters.name: Mapping method
parameters.description: Automatic or manual (extrusion-based) mapping when meshes do not match.

tools.notes: With Form Union no pairs are needed because the mesh is conforming. Pairs allow non-matching meshes and sliding (rotating machinery, moving parts) but add constraint equations and slightly reduce accuracy at the interface.

tools.name: Contact Pair
tools.description: Pair node defining a source (master) and a destination (slave) boundary set that may come into mechanical contact; the Contact feature in Solid Mechanics, Shell or Multibody Dynamics refers to it and adds the penalty or augmented Lagrangian contact equations. Requires Form Assembly. Choose the stiffer, coarser-meshed or concave side as source for best convergence.
tools.usage: Component > Definitions > Pairs > Contact Pair (p1); API: model.component("comp1").pair().create("p1", "Contact")

parameters.name: Source / Destination boundaries
parameters.description: Contacting surfaces; destination points search for the source surface.

parameters.name: Search distance
parameters.description: Manual or automatic distance within which contact is detected.

parameters.name: Mapping method
parameters.description: Automatic or extrusion-based initial mapping.

tools.notes: Form Assembly can create contact pairs automatically for faces within a tolerance (Create pairs > Contact pairs). Friction, adhesion, wear and thermal/electrical contact are subnodes or companion features that reference the same pair.

tools.name: Hide for Physics / View
tools.description: Component > Definitions > View nodes control the camera, lighting, axis and which geometric entities are hidden in the Graphics window; the Hide for Physics (Hide Geometric Entities) subnode hides domains or boundaries so you can select entities behind them when setting up physics without changing the model. Multiple views can be stored and referenced by plot groups.
tools.usage: Component > Definitions > View 1 > Hide for Physics (hide1); API: model.component("comp1").view("view1").hideEntities("hide1")

parameters.name: geometryEntities
parameters.description: Entity level and selection to hide (hideEntities(...).geom("geom1", 3).set(...)).

parameters.name: Camera subnode
parameters.description: Position, target, up vector, zoom, projection (orthographic/perspective).

parameters.name: Axis / Grid / Light
parameters.description: Axis limits, grid spacing, lighting and transparency for the view.

tools.notes: Hiding only affects display; use Filter or Selection attributes in plots to hide parts in results. Right-click a plot group and choose Copy View / Paste View to reuse camera settings between plots.

tools.name: Free Deformation (Moving Mesh)
tools.description: Moving Mesh definition feature (Component > Definitions > Moving Mesh) that lets the mesh in selected domains deform freely according to a smoothing equation (Laplace, Winslow, hyperelastic or Yeoh) driven by boundary displacements from the physics. It is the ALE machinery behind fluid-structure interaction, free surfaces, deforming electrodes and moving actuators. Boundary subfeatures (Prescribed Mesh Displacement, Prescribed Normal Mesh Displacement, Fixed/Free boundary, Symmetry) set how the mesh edges move.
tools.usage: Component > Definitions > Moving Mesh > Free Deformation (free1); API: model.component("comp1").common().create("free1", "FreeDeformation")

parameters.name: Selection
parameters.description: Domains whose mesh moves.

parameters.name: Mesh smoothing type
parameters.description: Laplace | Winslow | hyperelastic | Yeoh - Yeoh/hyperelastic tolerate large deformation better.

parameters.name: Boundary conditions
parameters.description: Prescribed Mesh Displacement, Prescribed Normal Mesh Displacement, Fixed Boundary, Free Boundary, Symmetry/Roller.

parameters.name: Automatic remeshing
parameters.description: Combine with Study > Time-Dependent Solver > Automatic Remeshing when elements invert.

tools.notes: Multiphysics interfaces such as Fluid-Structure Interaction and Two-Phase Flow, Moving Mesh add these nodes automatically. Deformed Geometry (same submenu) is the variant that changes the geometry frame instead, used for shape change by material removal/addition (etching, electrodeposition, shape optimization).

tools.name: Prescribed Deformation
tools.description: Moving Mesh / Deformed Geometry definition feature that moves the mesh in selected domains by an explicit displacement expression (e.g. a rigid translation of a magnet, a parametrised shape change) without solving a smoothing equation. Cheaper and more robust than Free Deformation when the motion is known analytically; the neighbouring domains then typically use Free Deformation to absorb the motion.
tools.usage: Component > Definitions > Moving Mesh > Prescribed Deformation (pres1); API: model.component("comp1").common().create("pres1", "PrescribedDeformation")

parameters.name: Selection
parameters.description: Domains moved rigidly or by expression.

parameters.name: Prescribed mesh displacement dx, dy, dz
parameters.description: Expressions in the material coordinates and time/parameters, e.g. 0, 0, v0*t.

tools.notes: Use Form Assembly with identity pairs when a moving part slides past a fixed one so the meshes do not have to stay conforming; for pure rotation use Rotating Domain.

tools.name: Rotating Domain
tools.description: Moving Mesh definition feature that rotates the mesh of selected domains rigidly about an axis at a prescribed angular velocity or angle (constant, expression, or time-integrated from a dynamic equation), the basis of rotating machinery models in magnetics (motors, generators) and fluid flow (mixers, pumps) together with Form Assembly identity pairs on the sliding interface.
tools.usage: Component > Definitions > Moving Mesh > Rotating Domain (rot1); API: model.component("comp1").common().create("rot1", "RotatingDomain")

parameters.name: Selection
parameters.description: Rotor domains.

parameters.name: Axis of rotation
parameters.description: Rotation axis point and direction (z axis by default in 2D).

parameters.name: Rotation type
parameters.description: Specified rotational velocity (rpm, rad/s, expression) or specified rotation angle.

parameters.name: Initial angle
parameters.description: Offset used for parametric/stationary sweeps over rotor position.

tools.notes: The Rotating Machinery, Magnetic (rmm) and Rotating Machinery, Fluid Flow interfaces add this node for you. The sliding interface must be a pair from Form Assembly; a Continuity / sector symmetry pair feature couples the fields across it.
